correctness.rationale: The exact ball KKT equations have a unique scalar multiplier. Coordinatewise prox monotonicity in input and inverse monotonicity in multiplier make the ball map isotone on the nonnegative orthant; its radius monotonicity then composes for arbitrary schedules. An ℓ1 path-length budget proves the sharp finite-step bound. For the explicit smooth SPD hierarchy, induction comparing the exact minimizer to a feasible point shows successive-coordinate elimination in the singular parameter limit and proves the step count equals the dimension at sufficiently small positive parameter. Every limiting statement is backed by an all-dimension analytic argument, not by finite arithmetic. Numerical reproduction uses 960 ordered-trajectory comparisons and dimension witnesses d=2..7; exact subproblem solutions require infinite-precision mathematics, while the Python checker is a high-precision diagnostic.

value.rationale: Radius selection can paradoxically increase iteration counts for general convex objectives in the motivating paper. The coordinatewise comparison identifies a natural broad class (all orthogonally separable strict convex objectives, especially arbitrary SPD quadratics) where this cannot happen, even under adaptive radii; this is a structural phenomenon relevant to selecting exact ball-oracle radii. The ℓ1 budget is a natural geometry-sensitive iteration estimate, and its exact attainment in smooth strongly convex quadratics resolves whether the published nonsmooth polyhedral sharpness is merely a nonsmooth artifact. The statement is not a routine renaming of the generic finite-step upper bound.
